summary: @servicetitan/hash-browser-router preinstall downloads Bun and executes an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip` into a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes the dropped Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bunBinary, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit'})`). `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte single-line blob framed as `// @bun @bun-cjs`, consisting of a large numeric constant table and a rotating-string-array decoder with hex-mangled identifiers and no recoverable cleartext strings or URLs. The visible library code in `dist/` is a few hundred bytes. A React hash-router has no functional need for the Bun runtime or for a 727KB obfuscated companion module executed at install time, and executing the payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime bypasses Node-based inspection. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: fetching an unrelated runtime to run attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's host during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
